mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in the past month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of FEDFUNDS decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past two months signals a weakening labor market, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over the past three months indicates strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of HOUST increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of INDPRO decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure that the Fed may address with tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher costs and reduced profit margins.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in a quarter and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.3% increase), it signals strong real demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL increases < 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong RSAFS growth and stable CPIAUCSL (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% in a quarter and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a strong supply-side response to accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 2% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 1%
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong supply response
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong INDPRO growth and low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).
